why: The app never suggests a next level: picker.ts has no 'suggested' state, so there is nothing to test. The criterion asks for behaviour that was never built.
Names `npm run guardrail:scan`, which does not exist in scripts/ or package.json. The no-identifying-data rule is enforced by review and the footer exception, not by a tool.
Nothing proves a full round works offline: the suite runs in happy-dom and never loads the built bundle. This needs the real-browser harness (proposal C), not a unit test.
Individual controls are asserted in picker and play tests, but nothing sweeps every interactive element for the 96 px rule, so a new undersized control passes.
Volume is not persisted and no size control exists; the app has a mute toggle only. Either the criterion is stale or the feature was dropped.
No scan of the built dist/ for third-party URLs. Proving it needs a build in CI and an assertion over the output, not over the source.

The app draws a single mascot (app.ts) and has no eight-mascot profile panel. The spec's own decision log still records 'Mascots | Keep', so this is a contradiction between two parts of the spec, not a missing test. It needs a spec decision before it needs a test.
`.limit-popup` was the reference design's level popup; the shelf replaced it in v1.2 and the styling no longer exists. Stale criterion.
`parity:check` does not exist as a script. The visual contract is enforced only by clockFace's palette test and by review; the screenshot comparisons were never automated.
Streak lives in the session; progress.ts has no bestStreak field, so there is nothing to persist. The criterion asks for a feature the app does not have.
